summary: The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is a transdisciplinary framework for children aged 3 to 12, built around inquiry rather than a fixed list of subjects. Each school plans its own programme of inquiry, organised around six transdisciplinary themes, so the framework does not publish a fixed topic list per grade. Learning draws on six subject areas and five essential elements (knowledge, concepts, skills, attitudes and action).
structure: Transdisciplinary framework for ages 3 to 12, built around inquiry.
Six transdisciplinary themes frame the units of inquiry: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet.
Each school writes its own programme of inquiry, choosing units that fit these themes.
Six subject areas are used inside units: language, social studies, mathematics, arts, science, and personal, social and physical education.
Five essential elements sit under the themes: knowledge, concepts, skills, attitudes and action.
